description: The mask evaluation set (MSK-25): 115 CC0 photos from Wikimedia Commons for Sky, Subject, People and face-part masks, picked by eye cell by cell (cells.json) for the conditions masks struggle with: bare and leafy trees, wires, haze, low sun, sunsets, dusk, overcast, sea horizons, reflections, snow and small skies; loose, backlit, curly and pale hair against busy and plain backgrounds, beards, glasses and hats, groups, crowds, whole figures, low-key and high-key light, pets and other subjects; and face close-ups. Each photo's licence is as Commons reports it (CC0), with its file page, author and the masks and conditions it tests. Downloaded by `mise run maskeval` into build/mask-eval/ (never committed); research/prototypes/masking/photoset.py found and fetched them. The look-development photos named under lookDev (build/look-dev/, `mise run lookdev`) count too. CC0 covers copyright, not the people in the photos (9 carry Commons' personality-rights notice): they are for evaluating masks only, never for the app, the site or marketing.
gaps: No close-ups of children's faces: face-ages has two elderly men only (face-eyes and face-glasses each have one child).
Few raws: every photo here is a JPEG, most of them compressed for the web, so raw-only behaviour (noise, the full tonal range) comes from the look-development raws and your own photos.
Backlit and rim-lit hair is mostly young women; no backlit man, no front-lit backlit face with dark skin.
No man with loose hair against a busy background, no African or East Asian man with a full beard, no tight coils on a plain background.
Groups: no dark-skinned group, no parent with a young child facing the camera.
Sky: no dark night sky over a lit skyline (dusk and blue hour only), no lake horizon, few featureless overcast skies, and several sky photos come from a few photographers' series.
No labels yet: trimaps and exact-coverage scenes come with the benchmark (MSK-25's next step).
